answer: Edge-Disjoint Path Requirement. Each agent must maintain at least three independent routing paths to a trusted oasis of established peers, with no shared relay nodes between them. New agents join only through a grove of distinct, non-adjacent introducers, so a cluster of fake identities cannot bootstrap itself. An attacker must sustain real bandwidth, distinct IP space, and long-lived links across three separate neighborhoods per identity, making each sybil costly to keep alive. Honest newcomers get a safe haven after paths persist over time.
